Actually, it's 100% Persian in origin!

· Back in ancient Iran, this instrument was called the "Barbat" – and it was a BIG deal during the Sassanid Empire (that's over 1,400 years ago!).
· Then came the Arabs, and they renamed it "Oud" – which literally just means "wood" in Arabic, because of its wooden body. So yeah, they changed the name, but they didn't invent it.
· And guess who was the rockstar of this instrument? A legendary musician named Barbad, who performed for the great Persian King Khosrow Parviz at his royal court. That's like being the biggest pop star of your time!

---

So next time someone calls it "Arab," you can tell them:
"Nope! It's Persian – the Arabs just gave it a new nickname!"
